newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Speculation shoves Colombian peso to softer close.
newsitem.headline: Speculation shoves Colombian peso to softer close.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed 2.7 pesos lower against the dollar at 1,046.25 on speculative trading and buying of U.S. currency by a state-run bank or financial institution, interbank dealers said.
"It seems like there was (dollar) demand from a state- owned financial outfit but there were also banks out there speculating with the exchange rate," one dealer said.
"It was speculation more than anything else," another trader said of the peso's fall. "We've talked to several banks and there wasn't any real demand (for dollars) from the corporate sector."

Most traders dismissed a new bout of political uncertainty stemming from Thursday's call by Vice President Humberto de la Calle for the resignation of President Ernesto Samper as a factor in the peso's decline.
Dealers reported 343 trades in Friday's session for a total of $140 million and said the peso held in a 1,046.95 to 1,044.50 range.
